sets.ref: hand: College-physics style example, 120 V to 100 kV with 50 primary turns and 10 A primary: N_s = 50 x 100000 / 120 = 41666.7; n = N_p / N_s = 0.0012; I_s = 10 x 120 / 100000 = 0.012 A = 12 mA; S = 120 x 10 = 1200 VA = 100000 x 0.012
hand: 120 V to 15 V with 200 primary turns: N_s = 200 x 15 / 120 = 25; n = 8; a 16 A secondary current needs I_p = 16 x 25 / 200 = 2 A; S = 120 x 2 = 240 VA = 15 x 16
hand: 12 kV to 240 V is n = 12000 / 240 = 50 (N_s / N_p = 1 / 50): U_s = 240 V; a 2 A primary current gives I_s = 2 x 50 = 100 A; S = 12000 x 2 = 24000 VA = 240 x 100

hand: Kuphaldt, Lessons in Electric Circuits vol. II ch. 9: a 250 V, 4 A heater (62.5 ohm) fed from 125 V through a 1 : 2 step-up transformer: n = N_p / N_s = 0.5; U_s = 125 x 2 = 250 V; I_p = 8 A so I_s = 8 x 0.5 = 4 A; the source sees n^2 x 62.5 = 15.625 ohm = 125 / 8 (impedance ratio 0.25); S = 125 x 8 = 1000 VA

solve.ref: hand: turns from voltages: N_s = N_p U_s / U_p = 200 x 15 / 120 = 25; I_p = 16 x 25 / 200 = 2 A
hand: U_p = U_s N_p / N_s = 15 x 200 / 25 = 120 V; I_p = 2 A
hand: turns from currents: N_s = N_p I_p / I_s = 200 x 2 / 16 = 25; U_s = 120 x 25 / 200 = 15 V
hand: zero primary turns: the number dimension refuses 0 (range), U_s and I_p divide by zero (not finite), and the turns check fires
